title: Hosted API — early warning thresholds and hedge behavior notes (P0)
content:
Summary:

This doc captures our field notes and a first-pass runbook draft after the hosted API P0 on 2029-08-29 where persistent p95/p99 latency spikes and streaming 5xxs occurred across multiple regions for ~38 minutes. The incident surface looked like a cascading interaction between the hedging layer, autoscaler hysteresis, and a telemetry ingestion lag that caused the global scheduler to mis-evaluate available headroom.

Impact:
- Duration: ~2029-08-29T18:11 -> 2029-08-29T18:49 UTC (38m)
- Affected customers: ~1.8k active tenants received degraded streaming sessions; non-streaming generation p95 increased 2-4x for ~45 minutes system-wide due to degraded multiplexing.
- Symptoms: elevated TTFB and stream stalls with intermittent 502s/504s from the edge->controller path.
- Severity: P0 (service-impacting across hosted API).

High-level hypothesis (why we think it happened):
1) Telemetry ingestion lag: metrics pipeline to the autoscaler was delayed by ~6 minutes due to a downstream Kafka partition imbalance (still under separate follow-up), so the autoscaler continued to assume higher free headroom than reality.
2) Hedge amplification: edge hedging (configured to hedge on slow first-chunk) started firing more often as prefix/KV cache miss ratio climbed, creating multiple duplicate live requests that increased backend RT and memory pressure.
3) Adaptive batching fallback: serving runtime detected increased per-request variance and autoscale signals were stale, so batching windows shrank and kernel selection moved to conservative (low-latency, low-throughput) paths — further increasing token cost and latency.
4) Small feedback loop: increased latency -> more hedges -> smaller batches -> more work per-token -> increased latency.

Observed metrics & traces (examples):
- Edge hedged fraction went from baseline ~4% to ~36% within a 5-minute window starting at 18:12 UTC.
- KV cache miss-rate increased from 7% -> 28% measured at the runtime layer at 18:10-18:16 UTC.
- Autoscaler perceived available headroom metric lagged by ~+6m compared to runtime load emitted timestamps.
- p95 TTFB (hosted-gen) rose from 320ms -> 1.1s at peak; stream session error rate spiked from 0.1% -> 4.7%.

Immediate mitigations taken (chronological):
- 18:14 UTC: Oncall toggled hedging rate limiter to cap hedge concurrency (stop-gap) — reduced hedging from 36% -> 15% over 4 minutes.
- 18:18 UTC: Rolled back a recent edge-side hedging config tweak (rollout id: r/o-2029-08-28-hedge) that had slightly lowered the hedging cooldown.
- 18:21 UTC: Manually increased dedicated fallback pool (hot-pool) capacity in us-west-2 by +20% to soak burst traffic while the autoscaler recovered.
- 18:30 UTC: Enabled a temporary streaming degradation flag (downgrade streaming to chunked polling mode) for highest-traffic tenants — reduced streaming 5xx and audience impact.
- 18:42 UTC: After Kafka partition rebalance and metrics pipeline catch-up, autoscaler view normalized; we reverted hot-pool bump and hedging cap at 18:48 UTC.

Root cause and contributing factors (final view):
- Primary root cause: telemetry ingestion lag (Kafka partition imbalance) leading to stale autoscaler signals.
- Contributing: aggressive edge hedging + recent config tweak without a rollback guard; lack of a hard cap on concurrent hedged inflight requests per-edge node; autoscaler hysteresis that is tuned for cost (slow to scale up) rather than fast emergency scaling.

Why existing alerts/early-warning didn't prevent escalation:
- Alerts are primarily based on autoscaler headroom signals which were stale; we lacked an independent, runtime-level early-warning metric (e.g., hedged_fraction or in-flight-session-queue-length) surfaced to paging.
- No circuit breaker for hedging amplification (we cap hedges per-tenant but not per-edge node).

Runbook: detection signals (first-pass)
- Page-on any of the following (thresholds are sketches):
  - hedged_fraction > 18% sustained for 3 minutes (global or per-region)
  - KV cache miss-rate > 15% with p95 TTFB rise > 200% vs baseline for 5 minutes
  - stream session stall rate > 1% and error rate > 1% compounded for 3 minutes
  - autoscaler_seen_headroom_delta > 3m (i.e., runtime timestamps > autoscaler lookback by >3m)

Runbook: immediate actions (playbook steps for oncall)
1) Rapid triage (first 5 minutes):
   - Verify telemetry lag: query runtime emitted timestamps vs autoscaler metrics ingestion timestamp (kafka offsets). If lag >3m, page infra-kafka SRE.
   - Check hedging fraction and recent hedging config rollouts (edge rollout id). If fraction > threshold, proceed to step 2.
2) Short-circuit hedging escalation:
   - Apply edge-level hedging cap (global override) to limit hedged concurrency per-edge node to configurable X (example X=6) for 15 minutes.
   - Revert any hedging cooldown config rollouts pushed in last 24h if correlation exists (rollback id if available).
3) Stabilize serving runtime:
   - Increase hot-pool (fallback) capacity by +15-25% regionally as a temporary soak.
   - If serving runtime batching moved to conservative kernels, manually set batching.window_ms to a moderate fixed value to encourage larger batches while telemetry recovers.
4) Degrade gracefully if needed:
   - Enable streaming-degrade-to-polling flag for top 10 tenants by qps.
   - As last resort, enable error-budget-based rate-limiting on non-core tenants.
5) Recovery validation:
   - Monitor hedged fraction, KV miss-rate, p95 TTFB returning to baseline for at least 10 minutes before reverting temporary caps/flags.

Playbook decision notes (operators):
- Hedging cap is preferred first because it limits request duplication without needing heavy infra ops. It is safer than immediately scaling up many GPUs (cost).
- Hot-pool bump should be limited-duration and owned by infra (who will roll it back once metrics show recovery).

Post-incident action items (owners + rough ETA):
- Aisha: ship hedging caps as a toggle in the edge config with per-node enforcement and a kill-switch (ETA: 2d).
- Marco: add hedged_fraction and in-flight-queue-length to the paging rules (alert + unmute) and add dashboard tiles (ETA: 1d).
- Lena: run Kafka partition rebalancing automated check and alert when consumer lag > 2m for autoscaler topics; add self-heal recipe (ETA: 3d).
- Daniel: tune autoscaler emergency scaling path to reduce upscaling hysteresis in critical SLOs (ETA: 1 week).
- Ravi: prepare a simplified incident runbook cheat-sheet for oncall to perform the 1–4 steps above (ETA: 48 hours).

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Was the recent hedging config tweak necessary? Need postmortem of the config change (owner: edge-pcfg).
- Can we add a kernel-selection canary indicator so the control-plane can detect when runtime falls back to conservative kernels and surface that as an early-warning?
- Investigate whether tenant-level hedging caps would have helped vs per-node caps; pros/cons on fairness.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally operational and slightly rough — please add clarifying runbook steps and make the hedging cap value prescriptive after engineering checks.
- If you were oncall and took any ad-hoc mitigation not listed here, paste what you did and timestamps so we can incorporate it.

Appendix (raw commands used in incident):
- Check hedging fraction: curl -s https://telemetry.internal/api/metrics?m=hedged_fraction|jq
- Query autoscaler lag: curl -s https://autoscaler.internal/debug/last_ingest | grep offsets
- Increase hot-pool: infra-cli pool adjust --region us-west-2 --pool hot-pool --delta +20%
- Toggle streaming degrade: runtime-cli feature-flag set streaming.degrade.polling true --tenants top10

End of notes.
